intro: ごと slices a stretch of time, space or a set of things into equal units and says something happens at, or differs by, each one. Its partner おき counts the gap between the times something happens. Most of the time they agree; they part ways with units you count one by one, such as days, where 一日ごと is "every day" and 一日おき is "every other day".

skills.rule: [number + unit] ごとに means "every (unit)"; [number + unit] おきに means "with a gap of (unit)", so with days, weeks and other counted units 一日おきに is "every other day".
skills.explain:
ごとに follows a number with a unit to say how often something repeats: 一時間ごとにバスが来ます (a bus every hour), 六時間ごとに飲む (every six hours). After a plain noun it means "each X, X by X", usually with differ or change: 国ごとに習慣が違う (customs differ from country to country), 季節ごとにメニューが変わる. Before a noun it becomes ごとの: 月ごとの売り上げ (monthly sales).

おきに counts the space left in between. With continuous measures such as minutes, hours and metres, the two mean the same: 五分おきに and 五分ごとに are both "every five minutes", 十メートルおきに is "every ten metres". With units counted one by one, such as days, weeks, people or rows, おき skips: 一日おきに is "every other day", 一行おきに is "on every other line", while 一日ごとに is "every single day".

Never add 毎 as well: 毎週 already means "every week". A verb + ごとに (会うごとに, "every time we meet") is formal; speech uses たびに.
patterns: [noun] ごとに 違う / 変わる  "X by X"

examples.jp: 一時間[いちじかん]{ごとに}バスが来[き]ます。
この薬[くすり]は六時間[ろくじかん]{ごとに}飲[の]んでください。
examples.en: Please take this medicine every six hours.

examples.jp: 国[くに]{ごとに}習慣[しゅうかん]が違[ちが]います。
examples.en: Customs differ from country to country.

examples.jp: 季節[きせつ]{ごとに}メニューが変[か]わります。
一日[いちにち]{おきに}ジムに行[い]っています。
examples.en: I go to the gym every other day.

examples.jp: 道[みち]の両側[りょうがわ]に十[じゅう]メートル{おきに}木[き]が植[う]えてある。
examples.en: Trees are planted every ten metres along both sides of the road.

contrast.note: ずつ shares out an amount, "X each, X at a time": 一人二つずつ (two each), 少しずつ (little by little). ごとに says how often or per what unit something happens: 一時間ごとに. Amount per person: ずつ. Repeat per unit: ごとに.
With counted units おき skips: 一日おき = every other day, 二日おき = every third day. ごと does not: 一日ごと = every day. With minutes, hours and distances they are interchangeable.
For "every time" after a verb, everyday speech uses たびに: 会うたびに. 会うごとに means the same but sounds written.

mistakes.bad: 一人[ひとり]{ごとに}二[ふた]つ取[と]ってください。
mistakes.good: 一人[ひとり]二[ふた]つ{ずつ}取[と]ってください。
mistakes.note: "Take two each" shares out an amount, which is ずつ on the number.

mistakes.bad: 一日[いちにち]{ごとに}部屋[へや]を掃除[そうじ]します。
mistakes.good: 一日[いちにち]{おきに}部屋[へや]を掃除[そうじ]します。
mistakes.note: For "every other day" use 一日おきに. 一日ごとに would mean every day.

mistakes.bad: 毎週[まいしゅう]{ごとに}会議[かいぎ]があります。
mistakes.good: 一週間[いっしゅうかん]{ごとに}会議[かいぎ]があります。
mistakes.note: 毎 already means "every". Use 毎週 alone or 一週間ごとに, not both.

skills.tip: Ask: is there a gap being skipped? Every other day or every second row is おき. Every hour, every country, every season is ごと.
